canada.title: Another storm expected for B.C., with 6,000 still without power from weekend weather
canada.summary: The third in a series of storms is heading for British Columbia, after wild weather knocked out power to thousands, triggered evacuations and left one person dead over the weekend.

canada.title: Amid national affordability crisis, northern Ontario's living wage rises to $21.35 an hour
canada.summary: People in northern Ontario need to earn $21.35 an hour to afford basic necessities, according to the latest calculation from the Ontario Living Wage Network, released Monday as part of Living Wage Week. A living wage is what's needed to cover expenses such as housing, food, transportation and child care, the network says.

canada.title: New Regina affordable housing project part of federal plan to end homelessness
canada.summary: Namerind Place, an Indigenous-led affordable housing project set to be built in downtown Regina, received $14.9 million in funding from the federal government. It's a part of Ottawa's plan to end homelessness in 10 years.

canada.title: Sweden says it won’t play Russia at world juniors as Norway faces losing spot
canada.summary: The Swedish Ice Hockey Association says it will refuse to play Russia if the teams meet at the world juniors, after being informed of a plan from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) to include Russia that could cost Norway its place in the Alberta tournament.

canada.title: Hellebuyck willing to face the music, but Devils say he won't play game in Winnipeg
canada.summary: It was supposed to be the grand, if a little awkward, return of Connor Hellebuyck to Winnipeg, but Jets fans will need to wait until another day to greet or taunt him.

canada.title: Inuvik killed dozens of grizzly bears at a dump this summer. Experts say it may have been the kindest option
canada.summary: This summer, over 28 grizzly bears were shot in Inuvik. While some people are now wondering why the Department of Environment has to ‘dispatch’ problem bears, instead of relocating them or leaving them alone, experts say death may be the kindest option.

canada.title: Calgary living wage up slightly from last year: report
canada.summary: The Alberta Living Wage Network says Calgary's living wage — or the amount a full-time worker needs to meet their basic needs, manage unexpected expenses and participate meaningfully in their community — is now $26.90, up from $26.50 last year.

canada.title: Mowi facing 8 charges over death at Stephenville hatchery in 2025
canada.summary: After a man died at a Stephenville hatchery in January of last year, charges have been laid against Mowi Canada East.

canada.title: B.C. lab ordered to pay $32K for misgendering transgender, non-binary patients
canada.summary: British Columbia's human rights tribunal found LifeLabs and its subsidiary Excelleris Technologies misgendered and outed three patients at clinics in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2019.

canada.title: OSAP pause may force dental college to close, school says
canada.summary: A spokesperson said evidence of systemic issues left the government with no choice but to pause OSAP payments to all private institutions to ensure the integrity of the system.

canada.title: Nova Scotia’s decision to extend freeze on HRM development fees has critics, but gets support from Andy Fillmore
canada.summary: Ecology Action Centre says costs for services will be handed down to public, while mayor says fee freeze will make housing more affordable.

canada.title: Report on 'critical challenges' in Lloydminster health care released by Alberta, Saskatchewan
canada.summary: An in-depth analysis that underscored “critical challenges” in Lloydminster’s health-care system has been released in full by the governments of Alberta and Saskatchewan, five months after the contents were deemed confidential.

canada.title: Tantramar Liberals oppose Holt’s Aulac toll plan
canada.summary: The Tantramar Liberal Association said in a Facebook post it is opposed to a provincial plan to charge a highway toll on New Brunswick's border with Nova Scotia. The association says tolls would negatively impact residents and businesses.

canada.title: Fredericton knitter uses yarn skills for international effort to save sea turtles
canada.summary: A Fredericton woman is one of six knitters chosen from around the world for a residency focused on sea turtle conservation.

canada.title: Future uncertain for Halifax home of Nova Scotia's first Black doctor
canada.summary: Community advocates are urging Halifax to preserve the historic North Street home of Dr. Clement Ligoure, Nova Scotia's first Black doctor, as the city acquires nearby properties to widen Robie Street for dedicated bus lanes.

canada.title: Behchokǫ̀ residents worry about health impacts of old uranium mine on Tłı̨chǫ lands
canada.summary: Multiple residents of Behchokǫ̀, N.W.T., say they are worried about the impact of a long-closed, but only recently remediated, uranium mine.

canada.title: Drug possession is illegal. Why can people use openly in public?
canada.summary: The drop in prosecutions — and the apparent rise in open usage — coincides with a Public Prosecution Service of Canada policy change in 2020 directing prosecutors away from laying criminal charges for drug possession, according to police officials and experts who spoke with CBC News.

canada.title: These moms fought to change Canada's 'discriminatory' EI Act — and officially won
canada.summary: The legal battle is finally over for a group of six Quebec moms who fought to have certain provisions of the EI Act changed. The federal government says it will not challenge a Federal Court of Appeal ruling in favour of the mothers who were denied job loss benefits after their maternity leaves.
